UNIT FRANCHISE AGREEMENT

THIS UNIT FRANCHISE AGREEMENT (this "Agreement") is entered into as of June 8, 2026 (the "Effective Date") between Copperlane Kitchens Franchising, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company with its principal place of business at 700 Marchmont Street, Nashville, Tennessee ("Franchisor"), and Rideau Hospitality Group, Inc., a Minnesota corporation with its principal place of business at 4425 Bellchase Avenue, Saint Paul, Minnesota ("Franchisee").

RECITALS

Franchisor has developed a system for operating fast-casual restaurants under the Copperlane Kitchens marks. Franchisee wishes to operate one such restaurant. Franchisor delivered its Franchise Disclosure Document to Franchisee on April 22, 2026, at least fourteen (14) calendar days before Franchisee signed this Agreement or paid any money to Franchisor, and delivered the completed copy of this Agreement on May 25, 2026, at least seven (7) calendar days before signing.

1. Definitions.

1.1 "System" means the business format Franchisor licenses under this Agreement, including the Marks, the Manual, recipes and specifications, unit design, training programs, supply-chain standards, and the point-of-sale and reporting systems Franchisor designates.

1.2 "Marks" means the trademarks, service marks, trade dress and logos Franchisor designates for use in the System, listed on Exhibit A.

1.3 "Manual" means Franchisor's confidential operations manual, in whatever medium Franchisor publishes it, as revised from time to time under Section 6.3.

1.4 "Franchised Business" means the single restaurant Franchisee operates under this Agreement at the Site.

1.5 "Site" means the location approved under Section 3.1 and identified on Exhibit B.

1.6 "Franchise Disclosure Document" means the disclosure document Franchisor prepares and delivers under 16 C.F.R. Part 436.

1.7 "Territory" means the area described on Exhibit B surrounding the Site.

1.8 "Gross Sales" means all revenue from the Franchised Business, in cash or credit, excluding sales tax collected and remitted, documented refunds to customers, and the face value of gift cards until redeemed.

2. Grant and Territory.

2.1 Grant. Franchisor grants Franchisee the right, and Franchisee accepts the obligation, to operate one Franchised Business at the Site using the System, for the Term. The grant is personal to Franchisee and is not a grant of an area development, master franchise or subfranchise right.

2.2 Protected Territory. During the Term, so long as Franchisee is not in uncured default, Franchisor shall not operate, and shall not license another franchisee to operate, a restaurant under the Marks with a physical location inside the Territory.

2.3 Reserved Rights. Franchisor reserves every right not expressly granted, including the right to operate and license others to operate restaurants under the Marks outside the Territory, to sell System products through grocery, wholesale and third-party e-commerce channels anywhere, and to use other marks for other business formats. Franchisor shall not solicit customers inside the Territory by direct mail or targeted digital advertising that names a location outside the Territory, except as part of a national or regional campaign.

2.4 No Exclusivity in Delivery. Delivery and catering orders may originate from and be fulfilled inside the Territory by other franchisees. Franchisee may likewise fulfill orders originating outside the Territory. Neither is a breach of Section 2.2.

3. Site, Development and Opening.

3.1 Site Approval. Franchisee shall submit a proposed location to Franchisor within ninety (90) days after the Effective Date. Franchisor shall approve or reject a proposed location within twenty (20) business days after receiving Franchisee's complete submission, and may reject it only on the criteria stated in Exhibit C. Franchisor's approval of a location is not a representation that the Franchised Business will be profitable there.

3.2 Construction. Franchisee shall build out the Site in accordance with Franchisor's approved plans, at Franchisee's expense, and shall open the Franchised Business within twelve (12) months after the Site is approved. Franchisor shall grant a reasonable extension for a delay caused by permitting, construction or an event described in Section 17.

3.3 Opening Conditions. Franchisee shall not open until it has completed initial training, obtained all licenses and permits, passed Franchisor's pre-opening inspection, and furnished the certificates of insurance required by Section 12.

4. Fees.

4.1 Initial Franchise Fee. Franchisee shall pay an initial franchise fee of $45,000 on signing. The fee is fully earned on delivery of the initial training and site-selection assistance, and is refundable in full if Franchisor rejects every location Franchisee proposes within the first year and Franchisee then terminates under Section 15.3.

4.2 Royalty. Franchisee shall pay a royalty of six percent (6%) of Gross Sales, payable weekly by electronic funds transfer on the Wednesday following the week measured.

4.3 Brand Fund. Franchisee shall contribute two percent (2%) of Gross Sales to the Copperlane Brand Fund. Franchisor shall administer the Fund for advertising, market research, and creative production for the System, shall spend contributions on those purposes and not on the sale of franchises, shall not be required to spend contributions in the Territory or in proportion to Franchisee's contribution, and shall furnish an unaudited annual statement of receipts and expenditures to any franchisee who requests it. Franchisor's own outlets contribute at the same rate.

4.4 Local Advertising. Franchisee shall spend at least one percent (1%) of Gross Sales on local advertising in the Territory and shall furnish proof of that spending annually. Franchisee shall submit advertising it creates to Franchisor for approval, and Franchisor shall approve or reject it within ten (10) business days; material Franchisor does not reject within that period is deemed approved.

4.5 Technology Fee. Franchisee shall pay Franchisor's actual documented cost of the designated point-of-sale, reporting and loyalty systems, which shall not exceed $500 per month, adjusted annually by no more than the increase in the Consumer Price Index.

4.6 Late Payment. An amount not paid when due bears interest at one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is less.

4.7 No Set-Off. Franchisee shall pay all amounts when due without set-off, except that Franchisee may withhold an amount that is the subject of a good-faith dispute of which it has given Franchisor written notice, and shall pay it within ten (10) days after the dispute is resolved.

5. Training and Support.

5.1 Initial Training. Franchisor shall provide initial training for Franchisee's principal and two managers at Franchisor's training center, at no additional fee, and shall provide an opening team at the Site for the first seven (7) days of operation. Franchisee bears its personnel's travel and lodging.

5.2 Continuing Support. Franchisor shall furnish the Manual, provide reasonable telephone and electronic support during business hours, visit the Franchised Business at least twice per year, and make available the supply-chain arrangements it negotiates for the System.

5.3 Additional Training. Franchisor may require additional training for a replacement manager and may charge its then-current fee, disclosed in advance, not to exceed $2,500 per person.

6. System Standards.

6.1 Compliance. Franchisee shall operate the Franchised Business in accordance with the System, including the standards for menu, recipes, portioning, food safety, uniforms, hours, cleanliness, guest service, and unit appearance stated in the Manual.

6.2 Approved Suppliers. Franchisee shall purchase products and supplies meeting Franchisor's specifications, from suppliers Franchisor approves. Franchisee may propose an alternative supplier, and Franchisor shall approve or reject it within thirty (30) days, applying the written criteria in the Manual and not withholding approval unreasonably. Franchisor may receive rebates from approved suppliers and shall disclose the aggregate amount annually.

6.3 Changes to the System. Franchisor may modify the System and the Manual, and Franchisee shall comply. Franchisor shall not require Franchisee to make capital expenditures exceeding $50,000 in any three-year period as a result of System changes, except for a change required by law.

6.4 Inspections. Franchisor may inspect the Franchised Business during business hours, with or without notice, and may conduct anonymous guest evaluations. Franchisee shall correct a deficiency Franchisor identifies within the time the Manual allows, and shall correct a food-safety deficiency immediately.

6.5 Refurbishment. Franchisee shall refurbish the Franchised Business once during the Term, in the eighth year, to the standard then applicable to new units, at a cost not to exceed $150,000.

7. Marks.

7.1 Licence. Franchisor grants Franchisee a non-exclusive licence to use the Marks solely in operating the Franchised Business during the Term, in the manner the Manual prescribes.

7.2 Ownership. Franchisor owns the Marks and the goodwill associated with them. Franchisee's use inures to Franchisor's benefit. Franchisee shall not register the Marks or a confusingly similar mark, or use a Mark in a corporate name, domain name or social-media handle without Franchisor's written consent.

7.3 Infringement and Defense. Franchisee shall notify Franchisor of an infringement or a challenge to the Marks. Franchisor controls the response and shall defend Franchisee against a claim that Franchisee's authorized use of a Mark infringes a third party's rights, and shall indemnify Franchisee for damages and reasonable attorneys' fees finally awarded or paid in settlement of such a claim, provided Franchisee used the Mark as directed.

7.4 Substitution. If Franchisor changes or discontinues a Mark, Franchisee shall adopt the replacement at Franchisor's expense for signage and printed materials, and Franchisor is not otherwise liable for the change.

8. Records and Reporting.

8.1 Reports. Franchisee shall report Gross Sales weekly through the point-of-sale platform Franchisor designates and shall furnish an annual profit-and-loss statement and balance sheet within ninety (90) days after its fiscal year end.

8.2 Audit. Franchisor may audit Franchisee's books relating to the Franchised Business on ten (10) business days' notice, not more than once per year except for cause. Franchisee shall pay the cost of an audit that reveals an understatement of Gross Sales of more than two percent (2%), together with the underpayment and interest.

8.3 Retention. Franchisee shall keep records relating to the Franchised Business for four (4) years.

9. Confidentiality and Covenants Against Competition.

9.1 Confidentiality. Franchisee shall keep the Manual, recipes, specifications, supplier terms and System know-how confidential during and after the Term, shall disclose them only to personnel who need them and have signed the form of confidentiality agreement in Exhibit D, and shall return or destroy them on termination. These obligations do not apply to information that becomes public through no fault of Franchisee.

9.2 In-Term Covenant. During the Term, Franchisee and its principals shall not own, operate or advise a fast-casual or quick-service restaurant other than the Franchised Business, except an interest of less than five percent (5%) in a publicly traded company.

9.3 Post-Term Covenant. For two (2) years after the Term ends, Franchisee and its principals shall not own, operate or advise a fast-casual or quick-service restaurant within five (5) miles of the Site or within five (5) miles of any other restaurant operating under the Marks on the date the Term ends. This Section is limited to what is necessary to protect the System and the goodwill in the Marks, and if a court finds its duration or area unreasonable, the court shall enforce it to the extent it finds reasonable.

9.4 No Solicitation. For two (2) years after the Term ends, Franchisee shall not solicit an employee of Franchisor or of another franchisee whom Franchisee learned of through the System, except through a general advertisement.

10. Transfer.

10.1 By Franchisee. Franchisee shall not transfer this Agreement, the Franchised Business, or a controlling interest in Franchisee without Franchisor's written consent. Franchisor shall not withhold consent unreasonably and shall respond within thirty (30) days of a complete request. Franchisor may condition consent on the transferee meeting Franchisor's then-current qualification standards and completing training, on Franchisee curing defaults and paying amounts due, on a general release from Franchisee, on the transferee signing the then-current form of franchise agreement for the remainder of the Term, and on payment of a transfer fee of $10,000.

10.2 Right of First Refusal. Before accepting a bona fide third-party offer, Franchisee shall give Franchisor a copy, and Franchisor may buy on the same terms within thirty (30) days. If Franchisor does not, Franchisee may sell to that offeror on those terms within one hundred twenty (120) days, subject to Section 10.1.

10.3 Death or Disability. On the death or permanent disability of Franchisee's controlling principal, the estate or representative has twelve (12) months to transfer the Franchised Business under Section 10.1, and the transfer fee is waived for a transfer to a family member who meets Franchisor's qualification standards.

10.4 By Franchisor. Franchisor may assign this Agreement to a party that assumes its obligations in writing.

11. Indemnification. Franchisee shall defend Franchisor against a third-party claim arising from the operation of the Franchised Business, and shall indemnify Franchisor for damages and reasonable attorneys' fees finally awarded or paid in settlement, except to the extent the claim arises from Franchisor's own negligence, from Franchisee's authorized use of the Marks, or from a System standard Franchisor required. Franchisor shall notify Franchisee promptly of a claim, and Franchisee shall control the defense with counsel reasonably acceptable to Franchisor. No settlement imposing a non-monetary obligation on Franchisor may be made without its written consent.

12. Insurance. Franchisee shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of at least $2,000,000 per occurrence, liquor liability if it serves alcohol, property insurance at replacement value, business interruption insurance, employment practices liability insurance, and workers' compensation at statutory limits. Franchisee shall name Franchisor as an additional insured on the liability policies, furnish certificates before opening and annually, and give Franchisor thirty (30) days' notice of cancellation.

13. Relationship of the Parties. Franchisee is an independent contractor. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship. Franchisee is the sole employer of its employees and alone controls their hiring, firing, scheduling, wages and working conditions; Franchisor's standards address the results of the Franchised Business, not the means by which Franchisee's employees perform their work. Franchisee shall post a notice at the Site identifying itself as an independent owner.

14. Term and Renewal.

14.1 Term. The Term is ten (10) years from the date the Franchised Business opens, unless terminated earlier under Section 15.

14.2 Renewal. Franchisee may renew for one additional term of ten (10) years if it gives written notice between twelve (12) and six (6) months before the Term ends, is not in uncured default, has substantially complied with this Agreement during the Term, refurbishes the Franchised Business to the then-current standard, signs the then-current form of franchise agreement (which may differ materially, including in the royalty rate) and a general release, holds or can obtain the right to occupy the Site, and pays a renewal fee of $15,000. Franchisor shall give Franchisee written notice at least one hundred eighty (180) days before the Term ends of any condition to renewal Franchisee has not met and of the time in which to meet it.

15. Default and Termination.

15.1 Termination by Franchisor Without Cure. Franchisor may terminate on written notice, without an opportunity to cure, if Franchisee abandons the Franchised Business for five (5) consecutive days without Franchisor's consent, is convicted of a felony that materially harms the System, makes a material misrepresentation in acquiring the franchise, repeatedly and knowingly understates Gross Sales, transfers in breach of Section 10, or becomes insolvent or has a bankruptcy proceeding commenced against it that is not dismissed within sixty (60) days.

15.2 Termination by Franchisor With Cure. For any other material breach, Franchisor may terminate only if it gives written notice describing the breach and Franchisee fails to cure within thirty (30) days, except that the cure period is ten (10) days for a failure to pay money and seventy-two (72) hours for a health or safety violation. Where a state franchise-relationship law requires a longer notice or cure period, that period applies.

15.3 Termination by Franchisee. Franchisee may terminate if Franchisor materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure within thirty (30) days after written notice describing the breach, or under Section 4.1 if no location is approved in the first year.

15.4 State Law. If a provision of this Section or of Section 14 conflicts with a franchise-relationship statute of the state in which the Franchised Business is located, that statute governs to the extent of the conflict, and this Agreement is modified accordingly for that franchise only.

16. Post-Term Obligations. On expiration or termination, Franchisee shall immediately stop using the Marks and the System, de-identify the Site including signage, decor and trade dress, cancel any assumed-name registration and transfer the telephone numbers, domain names and social-media accounts used in the Franchised Business to Franchisor, return the Manual and all confidential material, pay amounts due, and comply with Sections 9.1, 9.3 and 9.4. Franchisor may buy the furniture, fixtures and equipment at their depreciated book value by giving notice within thirty (30) days after the Term ends. Franchisor may enter the Site to remove the Marks if Franchisee does not de-identify it within ten (10) days.

17. Force Majeure. Neither party is liable for a delay or failure in performance, other than an obligation to pay money, caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, including fire, flood, earthquake, epidemic, war, terrorism, and a governmental act or order. The affected party shall notify the other promptly and use commercially reasonable efforts to resume performance.

18. Dispute Resolution.

18.1 Mediation. Before filing suit, other than for injunctive relief or for amounts due, the parties shall mediate in Davidson County, Tennessee, or in the state in which the Franchised Business is located if a state franchise law so requires, sharing the mediator's fee equally.

18.2 Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Tennessee, excluding its conflict-of-laws rules, except that a franchise-relationship or franchise-registration statute of the state in which the Franchised Business is located applies to the extent that statute requires.

18.3 Venue. The state and federal courts located in Davidson County, Tennessee have exclusive jurisdiction, except where a statute described in Section 18.2 requires suit in another forum, and each party consents to personal jurisdiction and venue accordingly.

18.4 Limitations. An action arising out of this Agreement must be brought within two (2) years after the claim accrues, or within the period a state franchise-relationship statute requires if that period is longer.

19. Limitation of Liability. NEITHER PARTY IS LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, OR FOR LOST PROFITS, EXCEPT FOR AMOUNTS PAYABLE UNDER SECTION 11 AND FOR LOST FUTURE ROYALTIES ON A TERMINATION CAUSED BY FRANCHISEE'S BREACH. FRANCHISOR'S TOTAL LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT IS LIMITED TO THE FEES FRANCHISEE PAID FRANCHISOR IN THE TWENTY-FOUR (24) MONTHS BEFORE THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM. These limits do not apply to Franchisor's indemnity under Section 7.3, either party's breach of Section 9.1, or either party's gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud.

20. General.

20.1 No Representations. Franchisee acknowledges that no representation about actual or potential sales, income or profits was made to it other than the financial performance representation in Item 19 of the Franchise Disclosure Document, and that it received and read that document. Nothing in this Section disclaims or requires Franchisee to waive reliance on a statement made in the Franchise Disclosure Document, and nothing in this Agreement waives a right or remedy a franchise statute gives Franchisee.

20.2 Notices. Notices must be in writing and are effective on delivery when sent by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by certified mail to the addresses in the preamble. A party may change its notice address on written notice.

20.3 No Waiver. A party's failure or delay in enforcing a provision is not a waiver of it, and Franchisor's waiver for one franchisee is not a waiver for another.

20.4 Severability. If a provision is held unenforceable, it is modified to the least extent necessary to make it enforceable, and the remaining provisions stay in effect.

20.5 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, with Exhibits A through D, is the entire agreement between the parties about its subject matter and supersedes all prior agreements and understandings about it. It may be amended only by a writing signed by both parties.

20.6 Survival. Sections 1, 7.2, 8.3, 9, 11, 16, 18, 19 and 20 survive expiration or termination of this Agreement.

20.7 Counterparts. This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one agreement.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have signed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.
